question.text: A uniform conducting wire of length is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>24</mn><mi>a</mi><mo>,</mo></math> and resistance <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>R</mi></math> is wound up as a current carrying coil in the shape of an equilateral triangle of side <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>a</mi></math> and then in the form of a square of side <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>a</mi></math>. The coil is connected to a voltage source <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>V</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>.</mo></math> The ratio of magnetic moment of the coils in case of equilateral triangle to that for square is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>:</mo><msqrt><mi>y</mi></msqrt></math> where <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>y</mi></math> is ____________.

solution.text:
4an1=24a

thus n1=6 turns

3an2=24a⇒n2=8 turns

M1M2=n1iA1n2iA2=6×a28×a2×34=31

M2M1=13=1y

y=3
